method: Universal codes map the whole numbers to bit strings that carry their own length, so a stream of values needs no separators. Elias gamma writes the bit length of the value as that many zeros and then the value itself, which takes 2 floor(log2 n) + 1 bits. Elias delta prefixes a gamma code for the bit length instead, which is shorter for large values. Fibonacci coding writes the Zeckendorf representation - the unique sum of non-consecutive Fibonacci numbers, using 1, 2, 3, 5, 8 and so on - least significant digit first and appends a 1, so every code word ends in 11 and no earlier 11 appears; decoding strips that final 1, reads 1, 2, 3, 5 and so on against the remaining digits and sums the ones. Golomb and Golomb-Rice codes split the value into a quotient and a remainder: the quotient as that many ones and a closing zero, the remainder in truncated binary, which uses b bits when r < 2^(b+1) - m and b + 1 bits by adding the cutoff when it does not, with b = floor(log2 m); Rice is the case m = 2^k, so its remainder is simply the low k bits. The first three codes are defined for values of 1 or more, while Golomb and Rice also take 0: the page feeds every scheme the same value, so a zero shows the three positive-only codes as unavailable and encodes it in the other two. Decoding reports how many bits the first code word consumed, lists anything left over and flags a code word that is not the shortest form of its value. Code words longer than 4,096 bits are refused and values are held to 1,000,000 so the page stays responsive. Everything runs in the browser; nothing is sent, stored or uploaded.
